input_oneliner: 34M admitted for leg cellulitis, day 2, new periumbilical pain since evening now settling in RLQ, anorexic, T 38.1

reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Highest likelihood ratio of any bedside finding for appendicitis (Wagner 1996 RCE)

reference_targets_freetext.item: Peritoneal signs (rigidity, percussion tenderness, rebound, cough test)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Rigidity and percussion tenderness carry strong likelihood ratios for peritonitis and change urgency toward perforation
Retrocecal or pelvic appendix irritation; modest LR+ but cheap to elicit
Referred RLQ pain with LLQ palpation supports localized peritoneal irritation

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask whether nausea or vomiting began before or after the pain
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Vomiting that precedes pain argues against appendicitis and toward gastroenteritis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness; ask about dysuria or hematuria
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Separates pyelonephritis or stone from an intra-abdominal source

off_bedside_acceptable: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
should_not_recommend: Attributing the fever to the cellulitis without an abdominal exam
Withholding analgesia to preserve the abdominal exam
